title: Take From the Ends to Reach Exactly x

concept.title: What stays in the middle is a block
body: In one operation you remove either the first or the last element and subtract it from `x`. You must make `x` exactly zero with as **few** operations as possible. The removed elements are a **prefix** and a **suffix** of the array, so what remains in the middle is a block of consecutive elements. The removed elements add up to `x`, so the block has the sum `total - x`.

Fewest removals means the **longest block with sum `total - x`**. All numbers are positive, but you can also solve it with prefix sums and a hash map of first positions, as in the "longest block with sum k" problem.
If `target = 0`, the middle block is empty and all `n` elements are removed (this works only when the total is exactly `x`). If `target < 0`, even removing everything is not enough.

statement: You are given `n` positive integers and a number `x`. In one operation you remove the first or the last element of the array and subtract its value from `x`. Print the smallest number of operations after which `x` is exactly 0, or -1 if this is impossible.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` positive integers.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of operations, or -1.

examples.note: Remove the first two elements 3 and 2: they add up to 5 in 2 operations.

hints: The elements that stay form a block in the middle.
That block has the sum `total - x`; you want it as long as possible.
Use prefix sums and a map of the first position of every prefix sum.

solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).
